hook: A $350M storage buy, cheaper AI video and open simulators
summary: Dropbox will buy AI storage startup Tigris Data for $350M, its largest deal yet, to power its new DBX Agent Cloud service.
Google DeepMind's Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash makes 15-second clips at $0.07 per second; Nvidia released four open-weight Cosmos 3 Nano checkpoints.
Mistral's Studio now deploys Le Chonk on cloud, VPC or on-prem, and Nvidia says codesign lifted agentic throughput per dollar up to 30x.

stories.headline: Dropbox to acquire AI storage startup Tigris Data for $350 million
stories.summary: Dropbox announced it will buy Tigris Data for $350 million, its largest acquisition to date. The deal gives Dropbox a cloud storage platform built for AI workloads and will be integrated into its new DBX Agent Cloud service.
stories.why_it_matters: The acquisition moves Dropbox from file‑sharing into AI infrastructure, giving developers a ready‑made storage solution for training and running AI models.
source_titles: Dropbox plans to acquire AI storage startup Tigris Data for $350M, its largest acquisition to date; Tigris raised ~$31.9M from Spark, a16z, and others (Mary Ann Azevedo/Crunchbase News)
Dropbox acquires Tigris Data for $350M to bolster its AI infrastructure
Dropbox Plans $350M AI Infrastructure Deal With Tigris Buy, Its Biggest Acquisition Yet
stories.line: Dropbox makes its biggest buy yet: $350M for AI storage firm Tigris
stories.detail: Tigris's storage platform, built for AI workloads, will be folded into Dropbox's new DBX Agent Cloud.

stories.headline: Google DeepMind launches Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash video model with 15-second clips
stories.summary: Google DeepMind announced Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, a generative video model that creates native 15‑second clips and supports multi‑turn conversational editing. The model is priced at $0.07 per second for 720p video, a 30% cost reduction from the prior version.
stories.why_it_matters: The lower cost and longer clip length make AI‑generated video more accessible for commercial content creation.
source_titles: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: Fast and cost-effective with longer clips
Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: Fast and cost-effective with longer clips
stories.line: DeepMind's Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash now generates 15-second video
stories.detail: Priced at $0.07 per second of 720p video, 30% below the prior version, with multi-turn editing.

stories.headline: Nvidia adds four open-weight Cosmos 3 Nano checkpoints for interactive simulation
stories.summary: Nvidia released four open-weight checkpoints—Cosmos3-Nano-Transfer-Auto, Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Auto, Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Transfer and Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Bimanual—each built on the 16-billion-parameter Cosmos 3 Nano model. They generate interactive world simulations and multi-sensor driving scenes.
stories.why_it_matters: The models give researchers and developers open tools to create realistic, multi-sensor simulated environments for robotics and autonomous-vehicle training.
source_titles: New NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Open Models for Interactive World Simulation
stories.line: Four open-weight Nvidia checkpoints for simulated worlds and driving
stories.detail: Each is built on the 16-billion-parameter Cosmos 3 Nano and can generate multi-sensor driving scenes.

stories.headline: Mistral launches Studio Le Chonk platform for enterprise AI deployment
stories.summary: Mistral AI announced that its Studio platform now supports the Le Chonk multimodal model, enabling enterprises to build and deploy agents, workflows and apps on cloud, VPC or on‑premises while retaining full control over data and infrastructure.
stories.why_it_matters: It gives businesses a way to use a large open‑weight model for coding, cybersecurity and document tasks without surrendering data sovereignty.
source_titles: Product Le Chonk brings the brains. Studio puts it to work. Build and deploy enterprise agents, workflows and apps faster, with control over your models, data and infrastructure. November 5, 2026 By…
stories.line: Mistral's Studio now runs Le Chonk for enterprise agents and apps
stories.detail: Companies can deploy on cloud, VPC or on-premises while keeping control of their data and infrastructure.

stories.headline: Nvidia uses full‑stack codesign to boost AI memory efficiency
stories.summary: Nvidia says its full‑stack codesign of GPUs, CPUs, networking, storage and software increases useful work per byte of memory. From Blackwell Ultra to the Vera Rubin platform, HBM capacity per GPU rose about 3% while agentic throughput per dollar rose up to 30× on SemiAnalysis AgentX.
stories.why_it_matters: Improving memory efficiency lets AI systems handle larger models and longer contexts without costly hardware upgrades.
source_titles: More Performance From Every Byte: How Full-Stack Codesign Solves AI’s Memory Challenge
stories.line: Nvidia credits full-stack codesign for more work per byte of memory
stories.detail: Agentic throughput per dollar up to 30x on AgentX from Blackwell Ultra to Vera Rubin; HBM per GPU up about 3 percent.
